numberItems.stem: For the N (tank) endorsement, what rated capacity must each individual tank have?
numberItems.explanation: Each individual tank must hold more than 119 gallons; 1,000 gallons or more is the aggregate (total) rule, and 500 gallons is the California flammable-liquid threshold (p. 8-1).

numberItems.stem: For the N (tank) endorsement, what total (aggregate) rated capacity must all the tanks on the vehicle add up to?
numberItems.explanation: The aggregate rule is 1,000 gallons or more; more than 119 gallons is the rule for each individual tank (p. 8-1).

numberItems.stem: [CA] An empty storage tank that is not built for transport is temporarily attached to a flatbed trailer. It is not a tank vehicle if its rated capacity is at least:
numberItems.explanation: California law (CVC §15210(r)) says an empty storage tank of at least 1,000 gallons, not designed for transport and temporarily attached to a flatbed, is not a tank vehicle (p. 8-1).

numberItems.stem: In the handbook's Figure 8.1, about how high is a tanker's center of gravity?
numberItems.explanation: A tanker's center of gravity is about 60–78 inches high, compared with about 18–24 inches for a pickup truck, which is why tankers roll over so easily (p. 8-2).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Extra speeding penalties apply to a tanker driver carrying more than how many gallons of flammable liquid?
numberItems.explanation: The California speeding rule (CVC §22406.5) applies to tankers carrying more than 500 gallons of flammable liquid; 119 and 1,000 gallons are the N endorsement numbers (p. 8-3).

numberItems.stem: [CA] A second speeding offense within 2 years while hauling a flammable-liquid tank load can suspend your HazMat or N endorsement for how long?
numberItems.explanation: A 2nd or later offense within 2 years brings a fine plus a suspension of up to 6 months; only a 1st offense is a fine alone (p. 8-3).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You drive a tank vehicle with a capacity over 500 gallons hauling flammable liquid. What is the most you may drive in a work period?
numberItems.explanation: The tank-vehicle rule (CVC §34501.2(b)(1)) limits driving to 10 hours in a work period; 11 and 12 hours are the general federal and California driving limits (pp. 8-3, 1-27).
